comparison: Perfect agreement on coarse-to-fine temporal dynamics (C17-C48). Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this finding aligns with established theories of visual processing and describe it as 'interesting.'

Strong disagreement on SF selectivity evidence (C15-C37). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with converging evidence from single-neuron and population analyses. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing concern that SF selectivity is observed 'for scrambled stimuli that drive the neurons poorly' and that responses are weaker than claimed.

Major disagreement on SF profile-category relationship (C23-C58 vs C21-C59). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with novel evidence from quadratic fitting and separability index. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, stating 'The conclusion that single-unit spatial frequency selectivity can predict object coding requires further evidence' and findings are 'premature given the low number of stimuli.'

Disagreement on population-level SF-category correlation (C21-C22, C59). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with high correlations (0.66, 0.39) and significant p-values. Peer reviewers challenge this as part of their broader UNSUPPORTED assessment of the SF-category predictive relationship, citing insufficient evidence.

Both address uncorrelated single-neuron mechanisms (C26-C27, C60-C61). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with near-zero correlations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting this finding contradicts the claimed SF-category relationship and contributes to skepticism about main conclusions requiring 'further evidence.'

Partial overlap on coding characteristics. OpenEval R6 addresses sparse SF coding (C28, C62-C63) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R5 covers broader temporal patterns (C28-C69) rated SUPPORTED. Both accept the methodological characterizations, with peer reviewers not challenging these findings.

Substantial overlap on temporal sparseness patterns (C29-C30, C64-C69). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with detailed temporal dynamics. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, consistent with accepted coarse-to-fine processing framework.

Agreement on CNN comparison findings (C31-C32, C70-C71, C102). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes comprehensive analysis across architectures. Peer reviewers do not challenge CNN findings, which align with their skepticism about the SF-category relationship in biological data.

Agreement on biological vs artificial differences (C33, C72). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval identifies key difference in SF profile-category relationships. Peer reviewers accept this finding, consistent with their view that the biological relationship itself is questionable.

Disagreement on response adequacy (C46-C47, C49). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting responses are above baseline with significant differences. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating 'the new data they provided confirmed my concern about low responses to their scrambled stimuli' - responses may be too weak for robust conclusions.

Agreement on small stimulus set limitation (C108). Both rate this as a valid concern. OpenEval notes SUPPORTED acknowledgment of limitation. Peer reviewers explicitly state findings are 'premature given the low number of stimuli they employed to assess category selectivity.'

Strong disagreement on stimulus duration (C125). OpenEval finds methodological details SUPPORTED as enabling reproducibility. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, identifying 'One big issue' that 'stimulus duration was too brief and could have weakened the effects of high spatial frequencies and confounded the conclusions.'

OpenEval finds category encoding validation (C73-C74) SUPPORTED with high accuracies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer concerns about stimulus set size indirectly relate to category assessment validity.
OpenEval finds cross-subject consistency (C88-C89) SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing data pooling from two subjects.

OpenEval finds interpretation about HSF processing (C90-C91) SUPPORTED with comparison to prior studies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer acceptance of temporal dynamics relates to this interpretation.
OpenEval finds methodological controls for confounds (C105, C122-C123) SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing low-level stimulus controls.
OpenEval finds class imbalance handling (C106-C107) SUPPORTED but notes circular reasoning. No corresponding peer review evaluation found on this methodological detail.

OpenEval finds background literature review (C1-C14) SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focus on empirical findings rather than literature review.

OpenEval rates speculative interpretations (C79-C86) as UNCERTAIN, noting hypotheses go beyond demonstrated evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these theoretical speculations.
OpenEval finds CNN mechanism differences (C85, C104) SUPPORTED but notes vagueness. No direct peer review evaluation, though peer R6 accepts CNN findings generally.
